54:1: God Almighty means by His saying, The Hour has drawn near, that the Hour in which the Resurrection will take place has drawn near. His saying, has drawn near, is derived from the verb to be near. This is from God Almighty as a warning to His servants of the approach of the Resurrection and the nearness of the end of this world. He commanded them to prepare for the horrors of the Resurrection before it attacks them while they are heedless and unmindful of it. And His statement, And the moon split, God Almighty says: And the moon split, and that was mentioned during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in Mecca before the migration to Medina. That was because the unbelievers of the people of Mecca asked him for a sign, so he, may God bless him and grant him peace, showed them the splitting of the moon as a sign and proof of the truth of his words and the reality of his prophethood. But when he showed them, they turned away and denied it and said: This is continuous magic. Muhammad has bewitched us. So God Almighty said: And if they see a sign, they turn away and say, ‘Continuous magic.’ The narrations came in a manner similar to what we said about that, and the people of interpretation said the same. Mentioning the narrations that were narrated about this and the report of those who said it from the people of interpretation: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada that Anas bin Malik told them that the people of Mecca asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to show them a sign, so he showed them the moon splitting into two parts. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad bin Jaafar told us: Shu’bah told us: I heard Qatada narrating on the authority of Anas, who said: The moon split into two parts. Ibn Al-Muthanna and Al-Hasan bin Abi Yahya Al-Maqdisi told us: Abu Dawud told us: Shu’bah told us on the authority of Qatada: I heard Anas say: The moon split during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Yaqub Al-Duraqi told me: Abu Dawud told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: I heard Anas say, and he mentioned something similar. Ali bin Sahl told us: Hajjaj bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, who said: “The moon split twice during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzaie told me: Bishr bin Al-Mufaddal told us: Saeed bin Abi Aruba told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas bin Malik (that the people of Mecca asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to show them a sign, so he showed them the moon in two halves until they saw Hira between them). Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abu Mu’ammar, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: “The moon split while we were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Mina, until a portion of it went behind the mountain. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Bear witness.” Ishaq bin Abi Isra’il told me: Al-Nadr bin Shumayl Al-Mazini told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Sulayman, who said: I heard Ibrahim, on the authority of Abu Muammar, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The moon split into two parts during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. One part was on the mountain and the other part was behind it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, bear witness. Ishaq bin Abi Israel told us: Al-Nadr told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Umar, like the hadith of Ibrahim about the moon. Isa bin Othman Al-Ramli told me: My uncle Yahya bin Isa told me, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Mina when the moon split and a group took refuge behind the mountain. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Bear witness. Muhammad bin Amara told me: Amr bin Hammad told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Aswad, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: I saw the mountain from the opening of the moon when it split. Al-Hasan bin Yahya Al-Maqdisi told us: Yahya bin Hammad told us: Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Al-Mughirah, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The moon split during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Quraysh said: This is the magic of Ibn Abi Kabshah, who has bewitched you. So they asked the travelers, and they asked them, and they said: Yes, we have seen it. Then God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed: The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The splitting of the moon has occurred. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Masruq, who said: Abdullah had five things that had passed: Smoke, Al-Luzum, Al-Batsha, Al-Qamar, and Al-Rum. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Ayoub told us on the authority of Muhammad: I was told that Ibn Masoud used to say: The moon has split. He said: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib told us on the authority of Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Sulami who said: We stopped in Al-Mada’in and were a farsakh away from it. Then Friday came and my father was with him. Hudhayfah delivered a sermon and said: God says: The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split. Indeed, the Hour has drawn near. Indeed, the moon has split. Indeed, the world has announced its parting. Indeed, today is the racetrack and tomorrow is the race. So I said to my father: Will you outpace the people tomorrow? He said: O my son, you are ignorant. Racing is only in deeds. Then another Friday came and we were present and Hudhayfah delivered a sermon and said: Indeed, God the Blessed and Exalted says: The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split. Indeed, the Hour has drawn near. Indeed, the moon has split. Indeed, the world has announced its parting. Indeed, today is the racetrack and tomorrow is the race. Indeed, the destination is the Fire, and the one who races is he who races to Paradise. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad bin Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of `Ata` bin Al-Sa`ib, on the authority of Abu Abd Al-Rahman, who said: I was with my father in Al-Mada`in. He said: Their leader delivered a sermon - and `Ata` used to narrate that he was Hudhayfah - and he said regarding this verse: The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split. The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split. The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split. Today is the racecourse, tomorrow is the race, and the one who races will go to Paradise, and the destination will be Hell. I said to my father: Tomorrow is the race. He said: Then tell him. Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut’im, on the authority of his father, who said: And the moon split while we were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Mecca. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Kharijah, on the authority of Al-Hussain bin Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of Ibn Jubayr, on the authority of his father: And the moon split. He said: It split while we were in Mecca. Muhammad bin Askar told us: Uthman bin Salih and Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told us: Bakr bin Mudar told us, on the authority of Jaafar bin Rabi’ah, on the authority of Arak, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Utbah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The moon split during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Nasr bin Ali told us: Abdul Ala told us: Dawud bin Abi Hind told us, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The moon split before the migration, or he said that had already happened. Ishaq bin Shaheen told us: Khalid bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, something similar. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-A’la told us: Dawud told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said regarding this verse, The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split. He said: That had happened before the emigration, and it split until they saw its two halves. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split… to His statement, continuous magic. He said: It has already happened. The moon had split during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Mecca, and the polytheists turned away and said, Continuous magic. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split, he said: They saw it split. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur and Laith, on the authority of Mujahid: The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split. He said: The moon split into two parts, one part remained, and the other part disappeared from the top of the mountain. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Bear witness. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid: “The moon split during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it became two parts. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Bakr: ‘Bear witness, O Abu Bakr.’ The polytheists said: ‘The moon was bewitched until it split.’” Ibn Hamid told us, on the authority of Mihran, on the authority of Abu Sinan, who said: A man came to Madain, stood up and said: God Almighty says: The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split. The moon has split, and the world has announced its separation. Today is the racetrack, and tomorrow is the race. The one who races will be the first to reach Paradise, and the destination will be Hell. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split. God will do whatever He wills to His creation. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, who said: The people of Mecca asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for a sign, and the moon split in Mecca twice. He said, The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And the moon split, that the split had already occurred during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Mecca, and the polytheists turned away from it and said: It is ongoing magic. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: The splitting of the moon took place in Mecca.
54:2: And His statement, And if they see a sign, they turn away. God Almighty says: And if the polytheists see a sign that guides them to the truth of the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and evidence that guides them to his truthfulness in what he brought them from their Lord, they turn away from it and turn away, denying it and denying that it is certainly true. And they say, denying it and denial that it is true: This is magic with which Muhammad bewitched us when it seemed to us that we see the moon split in two by his magic. And it is an ongoing magic. He says: An ongoing magic that will go away, from their saying, This magic has passed away, if it goes away. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Continuing magic, he said: Going away. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And if they see a sign, they turn away and say, ‘Persistent magic.’ He said: If the people of misguidance see a sign of God’s signs, they say, This is only the work of magic. It is likely that this will continue and then go away. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada, And they say, ‘Persistent magic.’ He said: Going away. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And they say, ‘Persistent magic,’ as the polytheists say when the moon is eclipsed: This is the work of magicians. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan, regarding his statement, Continuous magic. He said: When the moon split into two halves, one halve came from behind the mountain and the other halves went away, the polytheists said when they saw that: Continuous magic. Some of the people of Basra who were knowledgeable in the Arabic language interpreted his saying continuous as meaning that it is a mustaf’il from the verb imrar from their saying: Qad marra al-jabal meaning it became hard, strong, and intense, and amrartuhu ana meaning I twisted it violently. He said: The meaning of his saying And they say continuous magic is intense magic.
54:3: God Almighty says: And these polytheists from Quraysh denied the signs of God after their truth had come to them and they had witnessed the proof of their correctness by seeing the moon split into two halves. And they followed their desires. He says: And they preferred to follow what their desires called them to of denying that over believing in what they had become certain of the truth of the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the truth of what he had brought them from their Lord. And His statement, And every matter is settled, God Almighty says: Every matter, good or evil, has a settled ending, a settled conclusion, and a settled end. So goodness is settled for its people in Paradise, and evil is settled for its people in Hell. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And every matter is settled, meaning that good is for the people of good and evil is for the people of evil.
54:4: And His statement: And there has certainly come to them of the report that which is a deterrent. God Almighty says: And there has certainly come to these polytheists of Quraysh who denied the signs of God and followed their whims of report from the previous nations who denied the messengers of God as they are doing, and God brought down upon them of His punishments what is related in this Qur’an that is a deterrent for them. Meaning: And what deters them and restrains them from what they are continuing to do of denying the signs of God, and it is an active participle from the verb to restrain. And in a similar way to what we said about the meaning of that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, a deterrent, he said: the end. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And there has certainly come to them of the report that which is a deterrent, meaning this is a Qur’an. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan: And there has certainly come to them of the report that which is a deterrent. He said: Deterrent means the end.
54:5: And his saying, Conclusive wisdom, means by comprehensive wisdom: this Qur’an. And wisdom was raised in response to what in his saying, And there has certainly come to them of the report that in it is a deterrent. The interpretation of the statement: And there has certainly come to them from the report the report of which there is a deterrent of profound wisdom. If the word wisdom had been raised as a resumption, it would have been permissible, and the meaning of the statement would then be: And there has certainly come to them from the report of which there is a deterrent of profound wisdom, or it is profound wisdom, so the wisdom would be like an interpretation of it. His saying, So what use are vows? There are two interpretations of so what use are vows: One of them is that it means denial, so if it is directed to that, the meaning of the speech is: So the vows do not use them, nor do they benefit from them, because they turn away from them and deny them. The other is that it means: How, so the meaning of the speech, if it is directed to that, is: So what use are vows for them? And vow is the plural of vow, like new is the plural of new, and hasr is the plural of mat.
54:6: God Almighty means by His saying, Then turn away from them: So turn away, O Muhammad, from these polytheists from your people who, if they see a sign, turn away and say, Continued magic. For on the Day when God’s caller will call to the place of Resurrection, that is the most abhorrent thing.
54:7: With their eyes humbled He says: Their eyes humbled, without harm from them. They emerge from the graves which is the plural of grave, which is the graves. The Most High described the eyes with humbleness, not the rest of their bodies. What is meant by this is all of their bodies, because the effect of the humiliation of every humble person and the glory of every honorable person is evident in his eyes, not the rest of his body. Therefore, He singled out the eyes with the description of humbleness. And similar to what we said about the meaning of His statement, with their eyes humbled, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, with their eyes humbled, meaning their eyes submissive. The reciters differed in his saying with their sights downcast. The majority of the reciters of Medina, some of the Meccans and the Kufians read it as khasha’an with a damma on the kha’ and a shaddah on the sheen, meaning humble. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and some of the Basrans read it as khasha’an absarhum with an alif on the singular, taking into account the recitation of Abdullah. This is because in the recitation of Abdullah it is khasha’an absarhum and they added it, and it is the word of the noun in the singular, since it was an adjective by the rule of a verb, and it does in the singular if it precedes the nouns, as the poet said: And the handsome young men of Ayad bin Nizar bin Ma'ad So, he united the good and it is an attribute of the faces and it is plural and as the other said: The riders throw it into the open spaces, intercepting the necks of its prey and letting it slacken its grip. So it is singular and objecting, and it is a description of necks, and the plural and feminine are permissible in it, as we have explained. And His statement, As if they were locusts spreading out, God Almighty says: They will emerge from their graves as if, in their spreading out and striving to the place of reckoning, they were locusts spreading out.
54:8: And his saying, Rushing to the caller, means: Hastening with their gaze before their caller to that situation. We have explained the meaning of rushing with evidence that makes it unnecessary to repeat it, and we will mention some of what we did not mention in the previous narration. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Uthman bin Yasar, on the authority of Tamim bin Hudlam, regarding his statement, Rushing to the caller, he said: It means rushing. Ibn Hamid told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, Rushing to the caller, he said: rushing. He said: Mahran told us on the authority of Sufyan, Rushing towards the caller. He said: This is how their eyes are fixed on the sky. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Rushing to the Caller, meaning intending to go to the Caller. Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, rushing forward, meaning: looking. And His statement, The disbelievers will say, ‘This is a difficult day.’ God Almighty says: And the disbelievers in God will say on the Day when the caller will call to something reprehensible: This is a difficult day. They only described it as difficult because of the severity of its terrors and its confusion.
54:9: This is a threat from God Almighty and a warning to the polytheists of Mecca and all those to whom He sent His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for their denial of him. He has warned them that if they do not repent from their denial of him, he will bring upon them what he brought upon the nations whose stories he related in this surah of destruction and torment. He will save his Prophet Muhammad and the believers in him just as he saved the messengers before him and bought them from the punishment he brought upon their nations. So He, may He be glorified and exalted, said to his Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: You have lied, O Muhammad, before those who denied you from your people who, when they see a sign, turn away and say, Continuous magic, the people of Noah. They denied Our servant Noah when we sent him to them just as the Quraysh denied you when you brought them the truth from us and they said, He is mad. And he was warned, which is an active participle from zajarat. And this is what the Arabs do with the letter if it begins with a zay. They make the ta’ of the active participle a dal. From that they say: He was warned from… I rebuked and he declined from Zalfat and I increased from Zadat. The interpreters differed about the meaning of what they rebuked him for. Some of them said: Their rebuke of him was that they said: He has gone mad. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Yahya told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid: And they said, ‘He is mad,’ and he was warned. He said: He became crazy. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, with a similar chain of transmission. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, and he was deterred, he said: he was driven mad. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding this verse, And they said, ‘He is mad,’ and he was deterred, he said: He became very mad. Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi told me: Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us: Shu’bah bin Al-Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Others said: Rather, their reprimanding him and threatening him with cursing and stoning was with ugly words. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And they said, ‘He is mad,’ and he was warned, he said: They accused him, warned him, and threatened him that if he did not do so, he would be among those stoned. And he recited, If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among those stoned Ash-Shu’ara’ 116.
54:10: And His saying, So he called upon his Lord, ‘Indeed, I am overcome, so aid.’ God Almighty says: So Noah called upon his Lord, ‘Indeed, my people have overcome me through rebellion and transgression, and I have no power over them. So aid me through a punishment from You for their disbelief in You.’”
54:11: God Almighty says, So We opened when Noah called upon Us, seeking help from Us against his people, the gates of heaven with pouring water, which is gushing forth, as Imru’ al-Qais said in describing rain: The morning passed by, then a torrential downpour of rain descended upon it. The people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan: with pouring water. He said: It is poured out.
54:12: And His saying, And We caused springs of water to gush forth from the earth, God Almighty says: And We caused springs of water to gush forth from the earth. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan regarding his statement, And We caused springs to gush forth from the earth, he said: We caused water to gush forth from the earth and it came from the sky. And the waters met for a matter already decreed, he said, mentioning it: So the water from the sky and the water from the earth met for a matter already decreed and ordained by God. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan, Then the waters met for a matter that had been predestined. He said: The water of the sky and the water of the earth. It was only said: The waters met for a matter that had been predestined. The meeting does not happen from one person, but rather from two or more, because the water can be a group or one. What is meant by it in this place is: The waters of the sky and the waters of the earth, so the wording of the one was used, but its meaning is a group. It was said: The waters met for a matter that had been predestined, because that was a matter that God had decreed in the Preserved Tablet. Ibn Bashar told us: Muammil told us: Sufyan told us on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b, who said: Food was before bodies and destiny was before calamity. He recited: Then the waters met for a matter already decreed.
54:13: God Almighty says: And We carried Noah when the water met, on a command that had been predestined, in a ship of planks and nails. And nails is the plural of dasar. And it is sometimes said for its singular: dasir, just as it is said: habbak and habbak. And dasar is the nail with which the ship is fastened. It is said from it: dasarat al-sailin if you tighten it with nails or something else. The interpreters differed on this, and some of them said something similar to what we have said. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd told us: Ibn Lahi’ah told me on the authority of Abu Sakhr on the authority of Al-Qurazi, who was asked about this verse: And We carried him on planks and nails. He said: The nails are the nails. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, And We carried him on planks and nails. He told us that its nails are the nails with which it was fastened. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, of planks, he said: the planks of the ship. He said: and nailed: he said: and nailed with nails. Yunus told us: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And nails, that nails are the nails that were hammered into the ship and made it firm. Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, and nails, meaning: nails. Others said: Rather, the stern is the front of the ship. They said: It was described thus because it pushes and pushes the water. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us on the authority of Abu Raja’ on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement, And We carried him on planks and nails, he said: The water rolled down its eyes, or he said: its beak. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: Al-Hasan used to say regarding His statement, and a root: its root is used to root out the water. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of al-Hasan that he said: The water flows through her chest. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, and the hull. He said: The hull is the whole of the ship. Others said: The Dasr is the ship’s beam. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Hussain, on the authority of Mujahid: Of planks and nails. He said: The planks of the ship and the nails are its beams. Others said: The panels are its two sides and the two ends are its two ends. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Of planks and nails, that the planks are the two sides of the ship, and the nails are its two ends and its two ends. Others said: Rather, the ribs are the ship’s ribs. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, and the ribs, he said: the ribs of the ship.
54:14: And His saying, It runs before Our eyes, God Almighty says: The ship in which We made Noah sail runs before Our sight and view. It was mentioned on the authority of Sufyan in the interpretation of that: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan regarding his statement, It flows under Our eyes, meaning: by Our command, a reward for whoever disbelieved. The people of interpretation differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: Its interpretation is We cursed that as a reward for whoever disbelieved in it, meaning: disbelieved in God in it. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: A recompense for he who disbelieves. He said: Disbelieves in God. Al-Harith told me: Al-Harith told us: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid: A recompense for whoever disbelieved. He said: For whoever disbelieved in it. Others have interpreted the meaning of min to mean ma in this context and said: The meaning of the statement is: a recompense for the disbelief in God’s favors and blessings from those among the people of Noah whom He destroyed and drowned. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, A recompense for he who disbelieved, that he said: For he who disbelieved in God’s blessings and disbelieved in His favors, blessings, messengers, and books, then that is a recompense for him. The correct statement regarding this, in my opinion, is what Mujahid said, which is that its meaning is: So We opened the gates of heaven with pouring water and caused springs to gush forth from the earth, so We drowned the people of Noah. His divinity and His oneness, the people of Noah. Some of them said to one another: Do not abandon your gods, and do not abandon Wadd, nor Suwa’, nor Yaghuth, nor Ya’uq, nor Nasr. Noah 23. Whoever goes to this interpretation, it was from God, as if it was said: They were punished for God and for their disbelief in Him. If someone directed it to mean Noah and the believers in him, it would be a correct view, and the meaning of the statement then would be: We did that as a punishment for Noah and those who were with him in the ark, as if it was said: We drowned them for Noah and for what they did to Noah, what they did of their disbelief in him.
54:15: God Almighty says: And We left the ship in which We carried Noah and those who were with him as a sign, meaning a lesson and an admonition for the nations who came after the people of Noah, so that they would consider and learn a lesson and refrain from following their path of disbelief in God and denying His messengers, lest they be afflicted with the same punishment that afflicted them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And We have certainly left it as a sign, so is there any who will remember? He said: God left it in Baqirdi on the land of the peninsula as a lesson and a sign until the first of this nation looked at it with a look, and how many ships after it have turned to ashes. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And We have certainly left it as a sign, he said: God placed Noah’s ship on Mount Judi until the first of this nation reached it. He said: Ibn Thaur told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Mujahid that when God drowned the earth, He made the mountains rise, but Mount Judi humbled himself, so God raised it above the mountains and made it the resting place of the ship. And his saying, Is there any who will remember? He says: Is there anyone who remembers and remembers what we have done to this nation that disbelieved in their Lord and disobeyed His Messenger Noah and denied him in what he brought them from their Lord of advice, so that he may take heed from them and beware lest the punishment of God befall him because of his disbelief in his Lord and his denial of His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, like what befell them, so that he may turn to repentance and return to obedience. The root of mudkar is mufta’il from dhikra remembering. The fa’ of the verb, which is a dhal and a ta’, which is after the dhal, came together, so they became a doubled dal. The Arabs do the same with what begins with a dhal followed by a ta’ of ifti’al; they make them all a doubled dal, so they say: Idkartu idkar Idkartu idkar but it is actually idhkaru idhtikaran Idhkaru idhtikaran. Is there anyone who remembers? But it was said: Idkartu and mudkar because of what has been described. It has been mentioned from some of Banu Asad that they say mudkar in that case, so they change the dal and consider the dal and the ta’ to be doubled dhal. It has been mentioned from Al-Aswad bin Yazid that he said: I said to Abdullah bin Mas’ud Is there a male or female who is reminded? He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, taught me. Madhkur means with a stressed dhal. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, Is there anyone who will remember? He said: The one who remembers is the one who remembers. In the speech of the Arabs: The one who remembers is the one who remembers. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan: Is there anyone who will remind? He said: Who will remind?
54:16: And His statement, How was My punishment and My warnings? God Almighty says: How was My punishment for those who disbelieved in their Lord from the people of Noah and denied His Messenger Noah, and they persisted in their transgression and misguidance? And how was My warning of what I did to them of the punishment that I brought upon them for their disbelief in their Lord and their denial of His Messenger Noah, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him? And it is a warning to those of his people from Quraysh who disbelieved and a warning from Him to them that what befell the people of Noah of punishment will befall them for their persistence in their transgression. His saying and a vow means: and my warning, and it is a source.
54:17: And His statement, And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy for remembrance, God Almighty says: And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy, made it clear and detailed it for remembrance for whoever wants to remember, consider, and take heed. And We have made it easy. Muhammad bin Amr told us: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, We have made the Qur’an easy for remembrance, he said: We made it easy. Yunus told me: Ibn Hab told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy for remembrance, he said: We made it easy: We made it clear. His saying, Is there anyone who will remember? means: Is there anyone who will take heed and learn from what it contains of lessons and reminders? Some of them said in interpretation of this: Is there anyone seeking knowledge or goodness who can be helped in it? This is close in meaning to what we said, but we chose the expression that we used in interpretation of it because that is the most common of its meanings according to its apparent meaning. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember? He says: Is there anyone who seeks good to be helped in it? Al-Hussein bin Ali Al-Sada’i told us: Ya’qub told us: Al-Harith bin Ubaid Al-Ayyadi told us: I heard Qatada say about the statement of God, Is there any who will remember? He said: Is there anyone who seeks good and is helped to do it? Ali bin Sahl told us: Damrah bin Rabi’ah or Ayoub bin Suwaid or both of them told us on the authority of Ibn Shu’dhab on the authority of Matar regarding his statement, And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember? He said: Is there anyone who seeks knowledge so that he can be helped with it?
54:18: God Almighty says: The people of Aad also denied their prophet Hud, peace be upon him, regarding what he brought them from God, just as the people of Noah denied, and just as you, the Quraysh, denied your prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him and all his messengers. How was My punishment and My warnings? He says: So look, O people of the Quraysh who disbelieved in God, how was My punishment and My chastisement of them for their disbelief in God and their denial of His Messenger Hud, and My warning of My doing to them what I did in following their ways, and they were as they were in persistence in error and misguidance.
54:19: And His statement, Indeed, We sent upon them a furious wind, God Almighty says: Indeed, We sent upon the ‘Ad, when they persisted in their transgression and disbelief in God, a furious wind, which is a very strong, violent wind with a squeaking sound. It is taken from the intensity of the sound of its blowing when heard in it, like the way a speaker says: Squeak, and it was said from it: Squeak, just as it was said: So they were thrown down into it from So they were thrown down, and It squeaked from Nahanhat. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, a violent wind, he said: a cold wind. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, Indeed, We sent upon them a furious wind. Furious means cold. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: As-Sarar is the cold. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, a furious wind, that it is cold. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan, A violent wind. He said: Strong. Cold means cold. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, a furious wind, that furious means intense. His saying, On a day of continuous misfortune, means: On a day of evil and misfortune for them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Bad luck means misfortune. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about his statement, On an unlucky day, he said: Unlucky means evil. On an unlucky day means on an evil day. Others have interpreted it with a strong meaning. Whoever interprets it with that makes it an attribute of the day. Whoever makes it an attribute of the day should read it with the tanween of the day and the kasra of the ha’ from the word naha, so it would be in an unlucky day, as the Most High said, in unlucky days (Fussilat 41:16). I do not know of anyone who read it like that in this place, except that the narration that was mentioned in the interpretation of that from whom I mentioned it, as we described, indicates that that was a reading. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, On an ill-omened day, he said: Difficult days. Muhammad narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, On an unlucky day, that it means a difficult day. His saying, continuous, means: On a day of evil and misfortune, the affliction and torment continued upon them until they reached Hell. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: On a day of continuous misfortune that will continue with them to the fire of Hell.
54:20: And his saying, It will uproot people as if they were uprooted palm trunks, means: It will uproot people and then throw them on their heads, breaking their necks and revealing their bodies. Ibn Hamid told us: Salma told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq who said: When the wind blew, seven men from Ad went north, six of them from the strongest and most powerful of Ad, including Amr ibn al-Hilli, al-Harith ibn Shaddad, al-Hilqam, the two sons of Tayqan, and Khaljan ibn As`ad. They led their families into a valley between two mountains at night, then they lined up at the entrance of the valley to repel the wind from the families in the valley. The wind began to blow them away, man by man. Then a woman from Ad said: Time has taken Amr ibn Hali and the joys Then with Al-Harith and Al-Hilqam, the ascent of the two folds And He who blocked the wind from us during the days of calamities Al-Abbas bin Al-Walid Al-Bayrouti told us: My father told me: Ismail bin Ayyash told me on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq who said: When the wind blew, seven of the people of Ad stood up and said: Let us turn back the wind. So they went to the mouth of the pass from which the wind comes and stood over it. The wind began to blow and enter under one of them, uprooting him from the ground and throwing him on his head, breaking his neck. It did that to six of them and left them as God said: trunks of hollowed-out palm trees. And the bays remained. So Hud came and said: O Hud, what is this that I see in the clouds like the form of a camel? He said: Those are the angels of my Lord. He said: What will I have if I submit? He said: You submit. He said: Will your Lord chain me if I submit? He said: Woe to you! Have you ever seen an angel chain his soldiers? He said: By His glory, if he did, I would not be pleased. He then leaned over to the side of the mountain and took hold of a corner of it and shook it, and it shook in his hand. Then he began to say: Only the bays themselves remain. What a day yesterday! I have a firm footstep, and if he doesn't come to me, I will come to him and feel him. He said: Then the wind blew and caught up with him and his companions. Muhammad ibn Ibrahim told me: Muslim ibn Ibrahim told us: Noah ibn Qays told us: Muhammad ibn Sayf told us on the authority of al-Hasan: When the wind blew, the people of Ad rose up to it and took hold of each other’s hands as the Persians do and they thrust their feet into the ground and said: O Hud, who will remove our feet from the ground if you are truthful? So God sent the wind upon them and it made them like uprooted palm trunks. Muhammad ibn Ibrahim told me: Muslim told us: Noah ibn Qays told us: Ash'ath ibn Jabir told us, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: If a man from the people of 'Aad were to make two doors of stone, if five hundred of this nation were to gather together to do so, they would not be able to carry them. And if a man from them were to stick his foot into the ground, it would sink into the ground. He said: They are like trunks of palm trees. The meaning of the statement is: He will leave them as if they were trunks of palm trees that have been hollowed out. He omitted the mention of He will leave them because the statement indicates that it is sufficient. And it was said: He only likened them to trunks of palm trees that have been hollowed out because their heads were protruding from their bodies, so their necks would disappear and their bodies would remain. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us: Khalaf bin Khalifa told us, on the authority of Hilal bin Khabab, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, As if they were trunks of palm trees uprooted, he said: Their heads fell off like tents and their necks were spread out or separated. Abu Jaafar said: I am not sure, so he likened them to trunks of palm trees uprooted. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, People will be pulled out as if they were trunks of uprooted palm trees. He said: They are the people of Ad when the wind tore them apart and they were as if they were split palm branches uprooted.
54:21: So how was My punishment and My warnings? God Almighty says: So look, O group of disbelievers of Quraysh, how was My punishment of the people of Aad when they disbelieved in their Lord and denied His Messenger. That is God's way with their likes. And how was My warning to those whom I warned.
54:22: God Almighty says: And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy and simple for whoever wants to remember and take heed from it. Is there any who will remember? He says: Is there any who will take heed and be warned by its verses?
54:23: And His statement, Thamud denied the warning, God Almighty says: Thamud, the people of Salih, denied the warning of God that came to them from him. So they said, in denial of Salih, the Messenger of God, their Lord: Is he a human being from among us whom we, the large group, should follow, while he is only one?
54:24: And his statement, Then we would be in error and a Blaze, meaning: They said: Then we would be in error and a Blaze if we followed a righteous man, even though he is a human being like us. They mean going astray from the right path, deviating from the right path, and taking something other than the right path. And a Blaze: they mean by the Blaze: the plural of Blaze. Qatada used to say: What he meant by price is: the effort. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Then we would be in error and madness, in hardship and torment. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Indeed, then we would be in error and madness, he said: Error and hardship.
54:25: God Almighty says, informing us of what was said by those who denied His Messenger Salih, peace and blessings be upon him, from his people, Thamud: Was the Reminder sent down to him from among us? They mean by that: The revelation was sent down and he was singled out for prophethood from among us, and he is one of us, denying that God would send a messenger from among the children of Adam. And his saying, Rather, he is a wicked liar, means: They said, “That is not so. Rather, he is a wicked liar.” By wicked, they mean someone who is cheerful, arrogant, and haughty, and cheerfulness comes from activity. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Saeed Al-Qurashi told me: I said to Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Hammad: Who is the most evil liar? He said: The one who does not care what he says. The readers of the regions read it with a kasra on the sheen of ashr and a soft ra. It was mentioned on the authority of Mujahid that he used to read it as kadhdhab ash-shar with a damma on the sheen and a soft ra. This is in speech similar to al-hazir and al-hazir and al-ajal and al-ajal. The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is what the readers of the countries have said, due to the consensus of the authoritative readers on it. And His statement, They will know tomorrow who is the most evil liar, God Almighty says: God said to them: You will know tomorrow on the Day of Resurrection who is the most evil liar among you, O people of Thamud, and who was our Messenger Salih when you come back to your Lord. This interpretation is the interpretation of those who read it you will know with a ta’, which is the reading of the majority of the people of Kufa except for Asim and al-Kisa’i. As for the interpretation of that according to the reading of those who read it with a ya’, which is the reading of the majority of the readers of the people of Medina and Basra, Asim and al-Kisa’i.
54:26: For God said, They will know tomorrow who is the most evil liar, and He left out from the speech the mention of God’s saying, as the speech does not indicate it. The correct thing to say about this, in our view, is that they are two well-known readings, each of which has been recited by scholars among the reciters. So whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct, because their meanings are similar and they are correct in terms of grammar and interpretation.
54:27: God Almighty says: Indeed, We will send the she-camel that Thamud asked about the revival that they asked Him for. We sent her from them as a sign for them and an argument for Salih regarding the truth of his prophethood and the truth of his words. His statement, A trial for them, means a test and trial for them: will they believe in God and follow Salih and believe in what he called them to of the oneness of God when he sent the she-camel, or will they deny him and disbelieve in God? And His saying, So watch for them, God Almighty says to Salih: Indeed, We will send the she-camel as a trial for them, so watch for them and see what they will do with her. “And be patient,” He says to him: And be patient in watching them and do not be impatient and wait for what they will do with God’s she-camel. And it was said: And be patient. The root of the ta’ is a ta’, so it was made a ta’, and it is only ifta’ala from patience.
54:28: And His statement, And inform them that the water is to be divided among them, God Almighty says: Inform them: Inform them that the water is to be divided among them on the day of the she-camel's absence, and that is because she would come to the water one day and be absent the next. So God Almighty said to Salih: Inform your people of Thamud that the water on the day of the she-camel's absence was to be divided among them, so they would divide it up on the day of her absence, and they would drink from it that day and provision themselves from it for the day of her arrival. Some people have interpreted this to mean that the water was divided between them and the camel, one day for them and one day for her, and that it was said between them, and the meaning is what they mentioned, because when the Arabs wanted to report on the action of a group of human beings mixed with animals, they made the action an external one, as a group of human beings, because the action of the human beings predominated over the action of the animals. And His saying, Every drink is a temporary drink, God Almighty says: Every drink of water on the day of the she-camel’s departure and of milk on the day of its arrival is a temporary drink, they are waiting for it. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Every drink is prepared, he said: They bring them water when it sets and milk when it comes. Al-Harith told me: Al-Husayn told us: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Every drink is prepared, he said: They bring them to the water when it sets, and when it comes, they bring them milk.
54:29: God Almighty says: Then Thamud called to your companion, the one who had hamstrung the she-camel, Qidar ibn Salif, to hamstring the she-camel, urging him to do so. His saying, So he took hold of the camel and hamstrung it, means: So he took hold of the camel with his hand and hamstrung it.
54:30: And His statement, How was My punishment and My warnings? God Almighty says to the Quraysh 106:How was My punishment of them, the Quraysh, when I punished them? Did I not destroy them with the earthquake and the warnings? He says: How was My warning of those nations after them whom I warned of what I did to them and what punishment I brought upon them? And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me, my uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, So he seized her and hamstrung her. He said: He took her with his hand. How then was My punishment and My warnings? He said: It is said that he was born of fornication, so he is one of the nine who spread corruption on earth and did not reform. They are the ones who said to Salih, We will surely kill him and his family (al-Naml 27:49).
54:31: And His saying, Indeed, We sent upon them a single blast. We have previously explained the matter of the blast and how it came to them, and we have mentioned what has been narrated in this regard from the traces, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. And His statement, And they were like dry chaff, God Almighty says, “And they were, after their destruction by the blast, alive after their freshness, and their beauty before their destruction, like the dryness of the tree that you enclosed in a garden after its beauty and greenness, its leaf before its dryness.” The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of his saying, Like the chaff of the dying. Some of them said: What he meant by that is: the burnt bones. It is as if they directed its meaning to him being like these people after their destruction and affliction by the thing that a burner burned in his enclosure. Who said that? Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us: Abu Kudayna told us: Qabus told us on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Like the dry stubble of the dying. He said: Like burnt bones. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And they were like dry stubble, he said: burnt. It is not clear to us in this report from Ibn Abbas how he read it, except that we directed the meaning of his statement in the manner that came to us from his interpretation of his statement, like dry stubble, to the fact that he used to read it like the reading of the regions. And it is possible that his interpretation of it was like that, that his reading was with the opening of the Dhad of al-Muhtaḍar, on the basis that al-Muhtaḍar is an attribute of the stubble added to its attribute, as it was said, Indeed, this is the certain truth Al-Waqi’ah 95. It was mentioned from Al-Hasan and Qatadah that they used to read it like that and interpret it with this interpretation that we mentioned from Ibn Abbas. Abdul Warith bin Abdul Samad bin Abdul Warith told me: My father told me on the authority of Al Hassan: Qatada used to recite Kahshim Al Muhtadir meaning: burnt. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And they were like dry stubble, meaning: like burnt stubble. Others said: Rather, he meant the dust that falls from the wall. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Yaqub, on the authority of Jaafar, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: Kahshim al-Muhtadhir means the dust that falls from the wall. Others said: Rather, it is the shepherd's pen for the sheep. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, and he traced it back to him. He said: Al-Muhtazir is the shepherd’s pen for the sheep. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say, regarding His statement, Like the stubble of the enclosure, “Al-Muhtazir” means a pen that is made for sheep, then it dries up and becomes like the stubble of the enclosure. He said: It is the thorns that the Arabs use to surround their livestock from wild beasts, and the stubble is the dry tree that has the thorns of that stubble. Others said: Rather, he meant the shattered wood of the tent, which was broken. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told me on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Like the dry stubble of a dying man, he said: The man destroys the tent. Al-Harith told me: Warqa’ told us both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, Like dry stubble, dry stubble means a tent. Others said: Rather, it is the paper that falls from the firewood. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan Kahshim who said: Hashim: if you hit the barn with a stick, the leaves will shatter and fall off. The Arabs call everything that was wet and then dried Hashim.
54:32: God Almighty says: And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy to understand for remembrance. He says: For whoever wants to remember by it and take heed, is there any who will remember? By saying: Is there any who will take heed by it and consider it and refrain from what God hates in him?
54:33: And His statement, The people of Lot denied the warning, God Almighty says: The people of Lot denied the signs of God that He warned them of and reminded them of.
54:34: And His saying: Indeed, We sent upon them a hurricane of stones. God Almighty says: Indeed, We sent upon them stones. And His statement, Except the family of Lot, We saved them by magic, means: except the family of Lot, who believed him and followed his religion. We saved them from the punishment with which We punished his people who denied him and the stones with which We pelted them by magic, by a favor from Us. He says: a favor that We bestowed upon Lot and his family and honored them with it from Us.
54:35: And His statement, Thus do We reward the grateful, meaning: And just as We rewarded Lot and his family and bestowed blessings upon them, and saved them from Our punishment through their obedience to Us, thus do We reward the one who is grateful to Us for Our blessings upon him, so he obeyed Us and complied with Our command and what We forbade from all of Our creation. And He made His statement magic because it is indefinite. And if they said, I did this magic without a ba, they would not make it indefinite.
54:36: God Almighty says: And indeed Lot warned his people of Our punishment which had come before that. And they disputed about the warning. He says: So they denied his warning of that, out of doubt about it. His saying, They argued means they interacted from the verb mariyah. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: His statement, And they disputed about the vow, they did not believe him.
54:37: And His statement, And indeed they sought to seduce him from his guest, God Almighty says: And indeed the people of Lot sought to seduce him from his guest who had stayed with him when God wanted to destroy them. So We blinded their eyes, meaning: We blinded their eyes until We made them like the rest of the face, so that no slit could be seen in them, so they did not see his guest. The Arabs say: The wind has blinded the landmarks, if it buries them with the dirt it blows over them, as Ka’b ibn Zuhair said: From every fresh, mature woman, if she confesses, she will be exposed by the obliterated, unknown He means by his saying: The flags are obliterated: The flags are buried. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And indeed, they tried to seduce him from his guest, but We blinded their eyes. He said: God blinded the angels to them when they entered upon Lot. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And indeed they tried to seduce him from his guest, but We blinded their eyes. He mentioned to us that Gabriel, peace be upon him, asked permission from his Lord to punish them on the night they came to Lot, and that they tried to enter upon him, but he slammed them with his wing and left them blind, wandering about. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding the statement, And indeed they sought to seduce him from his guest, but We blinded their eyes, he said: When the people of Lot sought to seduce him from his guest, God blinded their eyes. He was forbidding them from the wicked deeds that they were doing, so they said, We will not abandon our deeds, so beware of hosting anyone or letting him stay with you, for we will not abandon him or our deeds. He said: When the messengers came to him, his wretched wife came out of the crack and came to them, invited them and said to them, Come, for there have come people whom I have never seen more beautiful faces, finer clothes, or purer spirits than them. They came running to him, and he said, These are my guests, so fear God and do not disgrace me in my guest. They said, Did we not forbid you from the worlds? Did we not come before you and excuse ourselves in what was between us? He said, These are my daughters, they are purer for you. Gabriel, peace be upon him, said to him, What frightens you about these? He said, Do you not see what they want? He said: We are messengers of your Lord. They will not reach you. Do not fear and do not grieve. We will save you and your family, except for your wife. You will do this matter secretly, and there will be a trial in it. Gabriel, peace be upon him, spread out one of his wings and blinded them with it, so they went around looking at one another. This is what God said: “So We blinded their eyes. So taste My punishment and My warning.” It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement, And indeed they tried to seduce him from his guest, that the angels came in the form of men, and that is how they used to come. The people of Lot saw them when they entered the village. It was said that they descended to Lot, so they approached them wanting to see them. Lot met them imploring them by God not to disgrace him in his guest, but they refused and came to enter upon him. The messengers said to Lot, Leave them alone and do not let them enter, for we are messengers of your Lord; they will never reach you. So they entered the house, and God blinded their sight, so they did not see them. They said, We saw them when they entered the house, so where did they go? But they did not see them and returned. And He said, So taste My punishment and warning. God Almighty says: So taste, O people of Lot from Sodom, My punishment that has befallen you and My warning with which I have warned other nations of punishment and examples.
54:38: God Almighty says: And indeed the people of Lot rose early in the morning: He mentioned that this was at the break of dawn. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan: Bakra means at sunrise. And His saying, punishment, which is turning the earth over with them and turning its top into its bottom with them, then following them with stones of hard clay, layered together. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan: And indeed, a torment overtook them early in the morning. He said: Stones were thrown at them. His saying, settled, means: That punishment will be settled upon them until the Day of Resurrection, until they meet God’s greatest punishment in Hell. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And indeed, a lasting torment overtook them early in the morning. A lasting torment overtook them, and it settled them in the fire of Hell. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And He overtook them in the morning Hud 78, Then He overtook them after this, meaning that God blinded their eyes, so they are in that torment until the Day of Resurrection. He said: And all of his people were like that. Do you not hear His statement when He says, Is there not among you a man of sound judgment? Hud 78 Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan: Stationary means settled.
54:39: And His statement, So taste My punishment and warning, God Almighty says to them: So taste, O people of Lot, My punishment which I have brought upon you because of your disbelief in God and your denial of His Messenger and My warning of you to nations other than you with the punishment I have brought upon you.
54:40: And His statement, And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy to remember, so is there any who will remember? God Almighty says: And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy to remember for whoever wants to remember by it, so is there any who will take heed and consider it, so that he may be deterred by it from what God has forbidden him to do and turn to what He has commanded him to do and permitted him to do.
54:41: God Almighty says: And indeed, there came to Pharaoh and his people Our warning of punishment for their disbelief in Us and in Our Messenger Moses, may God bless him and grant him peace.
54:42: They denied all of Our signs. God Almighty says: The people of Pharaoh denied the signs that came to them from Us and the arguments that came to them, that there is no god but God alone, all of them. So We seized them with the grip of the Almighty, the Powerful. God Almighty says: So We punished them for their disbelief in God with a severe punishment. No one with power can overcome what He wills, neither helpless nor weak. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, So We seized them with the seizure of the Mighty, the Compeller, meaning: Mighty in His vengeance when He takes revenge.
54:43: God the Almighty says to the disbelievers of Quraysh about whom God said that If they see a sign, they turn away and say, ‘Persistent magic.’ Are your disbelief, O people of Quraysh, better than those upon whom I brought My vengeance from the people of Noah, ‘Aad, Thamud, the people of Lot, and the people of Pharaoh? They hope to escape My punishment and vengeance for their disbelief in Me and their denial of My Messenger? He says: You are only in your disbelief in God and your denial of His Messenger like some of these nations whose situation I have described to you, and the punishment of God will descend upon you for your disbelief in Him, just as it descended upon them, unless you repent and turn back. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Your disbelievers are better than those, meaning those who have passed away. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hasan told us, on the authority of Yazid al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah: Your disbelievers are better than those. He said: Your disbelievers, O people of Quraysh, are better than those who have passed away. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, Your disbelievers are better than those, he said: Your disbelievers are better than the disbelievers whom We punished for disobeying God, and these disbelievers are better than those. And he said, Your disbelievers are better than those, he exhausted it. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Are your disbelievers better than those, or do you have immunity in the scriptures? He said: Your disbelievers are not better than the people of Noah and the people of Lot. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Abu Ja`far on the authority of Al-Rabi` bin Anas: Your disbelievers are better than those. He said: The disbelievers of this nation. And His saying, Or do you have immunity in the scriptures? God Almighty says: Or do you have immunity from the punishment of God, O people of Quraysh, that He will afflict you because of your disbelief in what the revelation from God brought you in the scriptures, which are the books? It was also narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Abu Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, The Books, that he said: The books. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, Or have you immunity in the scriptures? In the Book of God is immunity from what we fear. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah: Or do you have immunity in the scriptures? meaning in the books.
54:44: And His statement, Or do they say, ‘We are all victorious?’ God Almighty says: Do these infidels from Quraysh say, We are all victorious against those who intended to harm and harm us and wanted to fight us and divide our assembly?
54:45: Then God, the Most High, said, The multitude will be defeated, meaning the multitude of the infidels of Quraysh. And they will turn their backs, meaning: And they will turn their backs to the believers in God when they are defeated by Him. And it was said: The back, so he made it singular, and what is meant by it is the multitude, just as it was said, We struck their heads, meaning, We struck their heads, since the singular conveys the meaning of a group. Then God, the Most High, mentioned Him, fulfilled His promise to the believers in Him, so He defeated the polytheists in Him from Quraysh on the day of Badr, and they turned their backs. Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ayoub, who said: I do not know of it except on the authority of Ikrimah that Umar said when the verse, The host will be routed, was revealed: I kept saying, Which host will be routed? Then, on the day of Badr, I saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, jumping up in his armor and saying, The host will be routed and turn their backs. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Jaafar, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas: The army will be defeated and turn their backs. He said: On the day of Badr. He said: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, The army will be routed, meaning the army of Badr, and they will turn their backs. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, The army will be defeated.... “The verse tells us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the day of Badr, ‘They were defeated and turned their backs.’” Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, The host will be routed and they will turn their backs, that this was on the day of Badr. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Ayoub told us on the authority of Ikrimah: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would jump in his armor and say: The army has been defeated and has turned its backs.” Ishaq bin Shaheen told me: Khalid bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The multitude will be routed and they will turn their backs. He said: That was on the day of Badr. He said: They said: We are all victorious. He said: Then this verse was revealed.
54:46: God Almighty says: The matter is not as these polytheists claim, that they will not be resurrected after their death. Rather, the Hour is their appointed time for resurrection and punishment. And the Hour is more grievous and more bitter for them than the defeat they will suffer when they meet the believers at Badr. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: This verse was revealed concerning destruction. Their appointed time is the Hour. Then he recited, Your disbelievers are better than those… until His saying, And the Hour is more grievous and more bitter.
54:47: And His statement, Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness, God Almighty says: Indeed, the criminals are in deviation from the truth and are taken without guidance. And madness, He says: in burning from the severity of the suffering and toil in falsehood. As Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, in error and madness, he said, in hardship.
54:48: And His statement, On the Day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces, God Almighty says: On the Day these criminals are dragged into the Fire on their faces. Some of them interpreted His statement, On their faces into the Fire, as meaning into the Fire, and mentioned that this is in Abdullah’s reading, On the Day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces. And His saying, Taste the touch of Hellfire, God Almighty says: On the Day when they are dragged into the Fire on their faces, it will be said to them, Taste the touch of Hellfire. And leaving out the mention of it, it will be said to them, as the indication of the speech on it does not require mentioning it. If someone were to say: How can the touch of Hell be tasted? Its first taste is then tasted. This is disputed. Some of them said: It was said that way, as a metaphor for speech, just as one says: How did you find the taste of the beating? This is a metaphor. Another said: It is like what is said: I found the touch of fever, meaning the first thing that happened to me from it. Likewise, I found the taste of your forgiveness. As for Saqar, it is the name of one of the gates of Hell, and its ending was omitted because it is the name of a definite feminine.
54:49: And His statement, Indeed, We created all things with a measure, God Almighty says: Indeed, We created all things with a measure that We determined and decreed. This is a statement that God, may He be glorified and praised, threatened these criminals for their denial of predestination and their disbelief in it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention of who said: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Hisham bin Sa’d told us, on the authority of Abu Thabit, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he used to say: “I find in the Book of God a people who will be dragged on their faces into the Fire, and it will be said to them: ‘Taste the touch of Hellfire,’ because they used to deny predestination. I do not see them, so I do not know whether it was something that happened before us or something that will remain.” Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Rahman Ibn Mahdi told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ziyad Ibn Ismail Al-Sahmi, on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Abbad Ibn Jaafar, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, that the polytheists of Quraysh argued with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about predestination, so God revealed: Indeed, all things We have created with predestination. Ibn Bashar, Ibn Al-Muthanna, and Abu Kurayb told us: Waki’ bin Al-Jarrah told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ziyad bin Ismail Al-Sahmi, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ibad bin Ja’far Al-Makhzumi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The polytheists of Quraysh came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to dispute with him about predestination, so the verse was revealed: Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ziyad bin Ismail Al-Sahmi, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ibad bin Jaafar Al-Makhzumi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, in a similar manner. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Hisham told us: Husayn told us, on the authority of Sa`d ibn `Ubaydah, on the authority of Abu `Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, who said: When this verse was revealed, Indeed, We have created all things with measure, a man said, O Messenger of God, then what is the point of working? Is it for something we are starting over or for something we have already finished? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “Work, for everyone is facilitated for that for which he was created. We will facilitate for him ease and We will facilitate for him difficulty.” Ibn Abi Al-Shawareb told us: Abd Al-Wahid Ibn Ziyad told us: Khasif told us: I heard Muhammad Ibn Ka’b Al-Qurazi say: When the people spoke about predestination, I looked and saw that this verse was revealed about them: Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness... until His saying: We created it with predestination. Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Asim and Yazid bin Harun told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaab, who said: This verse was revealed only as a reproach to the people of predestination: “Taste the touch of Hellfire. Indeed, all things We created with predestination.” Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Salim bin Abi Hafsa, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b, who said: This verse was revealed only as a reproach to the people of predestination.
