He said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ziyad bin Ismail al-Sahmi, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ibad bin Jaafar al-Makhzumi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The polytheists of Quraysh came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to dispute with him about predestination, so the following verse was revealed: Indeed, all things We have created with predestination. He said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Hazim, on the authority of Usama, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, the same. Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Indeed, We created all things with measure, he said: God created all creation with measure and created for them good and evil with measure. The best of good is happiness and the worst of evil is misery. What an evil misery is. The Arabists differed about the reason for the accusative case of his statement, We created everything in proportion. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: Everything is accusative in the language of those who say, ‘Abdullah, I struck him.’ He said: It is common in the speech of the Arabs. He said: Everything is raised in the nominative case in the language of those who raise it and raised in another way. He said, We created everything in proportion. So he made We created it an attribute of the thing. Another said: “Everything is in the accusative case because his statement, ‘We created it,’ is a verb for his statement, ‘We,’ and it is more deserving of being presented to it than the object, so the accusative case was chosen. It is not said, ‘Abdullah,’ in his statement, “I struck him,’ is something that is more deserving of the verb. Likewise, ‘We ate your food.’ The choice is the accusative case because you mean, ‘We ate your food.’ Eating is more deserving of us than food.” He said: As for the statement of those who say, ‘We created it,’ an attribute of the thing, then it is far-fetched because the meaning is, ‘We created everything in proportion.’ This second statement is more correct in my opinion than the first, for the reasons that I mentioned to its author.
54:50: God the Most High says: And Our command for a thing when We command it and intend it to be is only a single word: Be, and it is, with no questioning therein and no desire therein. Like the blink of an eye. God the Most High says: And what We commanded and said to it, Be, is brought into existence, as quickly as the blink of an eye. It does not slow down or delay. God the Most High says to the polytheists of Quraysh who denied His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “And We have certainly destroyed your followers, O people of Quraysh, from among the past nations and past generations, for what you are upon of disbelief in God and denial of His Messengers. “So is there any who will remember?” He says: Is there anyone who will take heed of that and be warned by it.
54:51: As Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And We have certainly destroyed your followers, so is there any who will remember? He said: Your followers are from the people of disbelief from the past nations. He says: Is there anyone who will remember?
54:52: And His statement, And everything they did is in the scriptures, God Almighty says: And everything your followers who passed away before you, the infidels of Quraysh, did is in the scriptures, meaning in the books that the guardians wrote for them. It may be possible that what is meant by it is in the Mother of the Book. It was also narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, in the scriptures, that he said: the books. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And everything they did is in the scriptures, he said: The books.
54:53: God Almighty says: And every small and great thing is recorded. He says: It is recorded and written in the Book. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And every small and great thing is written down, meaning: It is written. So if God wants to send down a book, the scribes write it down. His statement, And every small and great thing is written down, means: It is written. Bishr told us: Ubaidullah bin Muadh told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Imran bin Hudayr, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: It is written on every line. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ubayd God ibn Mu’adh told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Imran ibn Hudayr, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: It is written. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And every small and great thing is recorded, meaning, it is preserved. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say: Mustartir means written. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And every small and great thing is recorded, he said: It is written. And he recited, “And there is no creature on earth but that upon God is its provision, and He knows its place of dwelling and place of storage. All is in a clear register.” Hud 6 And he recited, “And there is no creature on earth or bird that flies with its wings except that they are communities like you. We have not neglected anything in the register.” Al-An’am 38 It is a passive participle from I wrote a line.
54:54: And His statement, Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and rivers, God Almighty says: Indeed, those who feared God’s punishment by obeying Him, performing His obligations, and avoiding His sins will be in gardens and rivers on the Day of Resurrection. The word river is singular in its wording and meaning as plural, just as the word back is singular in its meaning as turning away in His statement, they will turn their backs. It has been said that the meaning of this is: Indeed, the righteous will be in spaciousness and light on the Day of Resurrection, so they directed the meaning of His statement, and river, to the meaning of day. The reciters claimed that they heard some Arabs chant: If you are Layla, then I am a river. When the morning comes, I do not wait. His saying river according to this interpretation is a source of their saying: I made rivers flow, a river. What he meant by his saying: For I am a river: is that I am a companion of the day: that is, I am not a companion of the night.
54:55: And His saying, In a seat of truth, means: In a council of truth in which there is no idle talk or sin. Beside a King, All-Powerful, means: Beside a King who has power over whatever He wills, and He is God, the Possessor of strength, the Mighty, Blessed and Exalted be He.
